words.meaning: Showing a lack of proper concern; nonchalantly dismissive.
words.example: His cavalier attitude toward exam prep worried our entire project group.

words.meaning: Relating to tailoring, clothes, or style of dress.
words.example: He upgraded his sartorial choices before heading to the corporate interview.

words.meaning: Cease to develop, flow, or advance.
words.example: My coding skills started to stagnate after I finished the basic Python module.

words.meaning: Gather or collect something, usually approval or information.
words.example: Her open-source contribution managed to garner attention from senior developers.

words.meaning: Secretly undermine the power and authority of an established system.
words.example: A clever algorithm can subvert the usual limits on query processing speed.

words.meaning: Move lightly and quickly, making a small sliding sound.
words.example: Notifications kept skittering across his phone screen while he drank chai.

words.meaning: Shock or excite someone into taking sudden action.
words.example: The sudden deadline will hopefully galvanize the team to finish the prototype.

words.meaning: Covered thinly with gold leaf or gold paint; superficially attractive.
words.example: That startup’s gilt promises masked a very shaky business model.

words.meaning: Prevent or hinder the progress of something.
words.example: Frequent power cuts tend to stymie our late-night coding sessions.

loop.meaning: An exclamation used when something unexpected, shocking, or wildly impressive happens.
loop.example: Bro dropped out to trade crypto and bought a Porsche, absolute bomba.
loop.context: Used widely among Indian youth in group chats when sharing wild gossip or flexes. Not rude at all.

loop.meaning: The initial period of a relationship marked by high affection, euphoria, and a lack of conflict.
loop.example: They are still in the honeymoon phase, they text heart-eyes emojis every two minutes.
loop.context: Brought up on podcasts and relationship advice reels when analyzing why a couple suddenly starts fighting after six months.

loop.meaning: Too Long Didn't Read, a short summary provided at the beginning or end of a massive wall of text.
loop.example: TLDR: The company rejected the merger and stock prices crashed.
loop.context: Used in text groups or comment sections when someone posts an essay instead of a normal message.

loop.meaning: The phenomenon where people believe media reporting on topics they don't know is accurate, despite knowing media gets their own specialized field completely wrong.
loop.example: You laughed at that fake tech news article, yet you still trust their political takes because of the Gell-Mann amnesia effect.
loop.context: Brought up in intellectual or media-critique podcasts when discussing journalism.

loop.meaning: A reaction phrase popularized alongside 'demure' to describe delicate or aesthetically pleasing things in an exaggerated way.
loop.example: Look at this stray cat sleeping on my notes, very cutesy, very mindful.
loop.context: Used ironically or sincerely on Instagram reels when showing off small pleasant moments.

loop.meaning: A street-smart, swaggering young man who hangs out on corners and breaks minor social rules.
loop.example: Stop walking like such a tapori and fix your collar before the interview.
loop.context: Classic Indian slang used playfully to describe someone acting a bit too street or rebellious.

loop.meaning: An inability or unwillingness to connect on a deep emotional level or commit to a partner.
loop.example: I keep dating guys who look great on paper but suffer from extreme emotional unavailability.
loop.context: A staple buzzword in modern dating discourse and therapy-speak reels. Can sound critical.

loop.meaning: Return On Investment, a metric used to evaluate the efficiency or profitability of an expenditure.
loop.example: Buying a gym membership is a great ROI for your mental health.
loop.context: Used by finance bros and business podcasts, but also jokingly applied to dating and daily life.
